title: The Lovers of the Banu Uzrah (తెలుగు)

full_text:
A merchant caravan traveling from Basra to Mecca halted for the night at a secluded desert oasis in the territory of the Banu Uzrah. While resting beside the water-channel beneath the date palms, the merchant heard a young Bedouin reciting verses of classical elevation, accompanying himself upon a one-stringed rebab.

The merchant approached and asked: 'Young warrior, who is the lady for whom you pour forth such sublime poetry?'

The youth answered with modest dignity: 'Her name is Mayya, daughter of our clan’s chief. We grew up together among the tents, our souls bound by shared reverence for truth, poetry, and honor. But her father’s herds were destroyed in a winter blizzard, and to rebuild his tribe’s fortunes, he has been compelled to accept the proposal of a wealthy emir of Syria.'

The merchant, deeply touched by their pure and sorrowful devotion, said: 'Has all hope vanished?'

The youth answered: 'Hope never vanishes while honor endures. We have sworn that though oceans of sand divide our paths, our thoughts shall remain pure and our loyalty unbroken. True love does not demand possession; it rejoices in the honor and peace of the beloved.'

The merchant was so moved by his noble character that he rode directly to the camp of Mayya’s father. He opened his caravan chests, weighed out two thousand gold dinars, and provided forty pedigree camels to restore the tribe’s herds, presenting them as a gift in the youth’s name.

The clan celebrated the union of Mayya and her faithful poet with ten days of joyous festivities, and the merchant departed with a joyful heart, knowing that generosity had preserved the sacred covenant of the Banu Uzrah.
moral: Chaste affection and steadfast fidelity shine like unmoving stars across the shifting desert sands. [TE]
